stances.claim: The SC's Dec 10 2013 motu proprio resolution institutes five pro hac vice measures to hasten the Maguindanao massacre trial -- directing JAR implementation despite its prosecutor-requested suspension, enjoining separate trials and installment decisions to avoid decades-long single judgment, designating a third assisting judge for nontrial incidents, and authorizing resolution of motions despite higher-court pendency.

Items 2 and 3 (separate trials + installment decisions) are very important because, ordinarily, judgments are rendered only after all testimonial and documentary evidence for and against ALL accused -- given the numerous accused, witnesses, and voluminous documents, this would take decades for a single final judgment.
stances.rhetorical_move: decades-otherwise impossibility argument for installment-judgment innovation

stances.claim: Item 5 (resolve motions despite higher-court pendency) is procedurally significant because normally trial courts stop in deference to higher courts when interlocutory orders are challenged on appeal, indefinitely delaying trials.

The Maguindanao massacre cases are a litmus test of our judicial system and the officials tending it -- especially the President and the justices -- and the SC directives raise fresh hopes that the cases will move much faster with partial judgments rendered soon on some accused.

notable_anecdotes: The stark stats catalog -- 71 case-record volumes, 38 TSN volumes, 139 witnesses, 560 petitions/motions, 427 resolved, 64 accused petitioning for bail (8 Ampatuans + 42 police officers + 14 civilians) represented by 39 sets of lawyers -- among the most concentrated procedural-scale stats in the corpus, used to anchor the 'intimidating and unprecedented' framing.

The 'back-hoed' detail -- the most visceral single word in the column, describing how the 58 defenseless civilians were disposed of, deployed to remind readers of the case's moral gravity before the procedural exposition.

The JAR effectivity-suspension reversal -- promulgated Sept 4 2012, suspended at public-prosecutor request for lack of time/personnel, now implemented for Maguindanao despite the suspension -- the Court's most pointed procedural intervention.

The 'in installments' framing for judgment delivery -- Ampatuans first, then some policemen, etc., while proceedings against others still at large continue -- a procedural innovation unique to this resolution.

Harry Roque's tripartite pro bono effort -- criminal-case representation + AMLC asset-freeze petition + NAPOLCOM administrative-dismissal charges -- captured concisely as a model of private-prosecutor multi-front strategy.
Three of the accused have died -- a fact stated baldly without comment, but with implicit weight for the four-year procedural arc.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban reports the Supreme Court's Dec 10 2013 motu proprio resolution instituting five new pro hac vice measures to speed up the Maguindanao massacre trial. He recaps the Nov 23 2009 atrocity -- the most gruesome crime of our time, 58 defenseless civilians (34 media workers) shot, mangled, killed, and back-hoed; 197 accused in 58 separate informations originally filed in RTC Maguindanao but transferred to RTC Quezon City Branch 221 under Judge Jocelyn Solis-Reyes with two assisting judges. Status: 3 accused dead, 194 remaining, 106 detained without bail for capital murder, 88 still at large. The procedural scale is intimidating and unprecedented -- 71 case-record volumes, 38 TSN volumes, 139 witnesses, 560 petitions/motions/manifestations filed (427 resolved), with 64 accused petitioning for bail (8 Ampatuans + 42 police officers + 14 civilians) represented by 39 sets of lawyers. The five SC guidelines: (1) DIRECT implementation of the Judicial Affidavit Rule (promulgated Sept 4 2012 but suspended at the public prosecutors' request -- the Court overrides for Maguindanao); (2) ENJOIN the presiding judge to hold, based on her discretion, separate trials for accused against whom no further prosecution evidence is contemplated; (3) AUTHORIZE separate decisions in any of the 58 cases without waiting for completion of evidence-for-all-accused -- items 2 and 3 are very important because ordinarily a single final judgment would take decades, but under these guidelines judgments can be issued 'in installments' (Ampatuans first, then some policemen, etc.); (4) DESIGNATE a third assisting judge for nontrial incidents like arraignment and pretrials so Judge Solis-Reyes can focus on trials; (5) AUTHORIZE the presiding and assisting judges to resolve motions despite higher-court pendency -- overriding the normal stop-in-deference rule that indefinitely delays trials. Harry Roque, pro bono private prosecutor for 15 media workers and 2 others, hailed the directives and asked the Executive to do its share, also petitioning the AMLC for asset freezes and filing NAPOLCOM administrative-dismissal charges against accused policemen. Panganiban frames the cases as a litmus test of the judicial system and its officials, and the SC directives as raising fresh hopes that the cases will move much faster with partial judgments soon on some accused.
